# The statement says "the winner ... ended two point under par ( - 2)", which likely refers to the specific occurrence where to par is "- 2".
# We'll filter for rows where tournament contains the relevant substring and to par equals "- 2".

# Filter rows where tournament contains "miyagi tv cup" and "dunlop ladies open"
filtered = df[df['tournament'].str.contains('miyagi tv cup', case=False, na=False) & 
              df['tournament'].str.contains('dunlop ladies open', case=False, na=False)]

# Check if any of these rows have to par exactly equal to "- 2"
# The to par column in the table shows values like "- 5", "- 10", etc., with a space after the minus.
# We compare exactly as it appears.
has_minus_two = (filtered['to par'] == '- 2').any()

# Assign the result to answer
answer = bool(has_minus_two)
